status: Staged author-level source review; independent clinical validation and empirical difficulty evaluation pending

items.sourceUse: Treatment of susceptible bacterial infections. Palestinian product information includes respiratory, urinary/kidney, and skin/soft-tissue infections; use should match the actual infection, culture data and local antimicrobial plan.
items.stem: Which infection plan best fits a prescribed levofloxacin course when culture susceptibility and local guidance support its use?
items.correct: Treating a susceptible bacterial kidney infection
alternatives: Treating uncomplicated asymptomatic bacteriuria without an indication
Treating candidemia documented by a positive blood culture
Treating influenza without evidence of bacterial infection

items.sourceUse: Prevention/control of angina; not the rapid-rescue formulation for an acute angina attack.
items.stem: Which prescribed treatment goal best matches an oral maintenance isosorbide mononitrate formulation?
items.correct: Preventing recurrent exertional angina over time
alternatives: Immediately terminating chest pain during an acute attack
Restoring arterial pressure during cardiogenic hypotension
Rapidly restoring coronary flow after an occlusive thrombus

items.sourceUse: Faster nitrate relief than long-acting oral isosorbide mononitrate; IV nitrate therapy may be used for severe/unstable angina or refractory LV failure when specifically ordered.
items.stem: Which situation best matches a prescribed monitored IV isosorbide dinitrate treatment?
items.correct: Severe ischemic chest discomfort with adequate pressure requiring nitrate therapy
alternatives: Chest discomfort with systolic BP 75 mmHg after a PDE-5 inhibitor
Pulseless ventricular fibrillation requiring defibrillation
Acute coronary occlusion when nitrate is proposed instead of reperfusion

items.sourceUse: Anticoagulation for selected thromboembolic/ACS indications according to the order; same family as enoxaparin but a different molecule/product.
items.stem: Which statement accurately describes the prescribed role of nadroparin in thromboembolic care?
items.correct: It provides anticoagulation without directly dissolving an established clot
alternatives: It produces fibrinolysis to rapidly dissolve an obstructive thrombus
It neutralizes warfarin anticoagulation during major bleeding
It replaces enoxaparin at the same syringe dose without reassessment

items.sourceUse: Anticoagulation in ACS and other thromboembolic indications according to the written order/protocol.
items.stem: A patient with acute coronary syndrome receives prescribed enoxaparin. Which role best explains its use?
items.correct: Reducing thrombus propagation as part of an antithrombotic plan
alternatives: Rapidly dissolving an existing coronary clot by fibrinolysis
Replacing indicated antiplatelet therapy as the only ACS treatment
Treating chest pain directly by relaxing coronary arteries

items.sourceUse: Same drug at different doses. Low-dose aspirin ('baby aspirin') usually means about 75–100 mg daily and is used mainly for antiplatelet effect when indicated. Higher aspirin doses are used for analgesic/antipyretic or anti-inflammatory effects depending on the indication and product.
items.stem: Which prescription purpose most specifically matches daily low-dose aspirin after ACS?
items.correct: Long-term inhibition of platelet aggregation
alternatives: Direct inhibition of thrombin during a heparin infusion
Replacement of clotting factors during active hemorrhage
Treatment of an infected coronary stent with an antimicrobial

items.sourceUse: Commonly part of dual antiplatelet therapy after ACS/PCI and coronary stenting.
items.stem: A patient has a recent coronary stent. Which treatment goal most directly explains prescribed clopidogrel?
items.correct: Reducing stent-associated platelet thrombosis risk
alternatives: Directly dissolving a stent thrombus already blocking blood flow
Treating restenosis by lowering LDL cholesterol
Providing acute anticoagulation by blocking factor Xa

items.sourceUse: Rate/BP control and reduction of cardiac workload in selected cardiovascular patients.
items.stem: Which clinical goal is consistent with oral bisoprolol in an appropriately selected cardiovascular patient?
items.correct: Controlling heart rate and reducing cardiac workload
alternatives: Increasing myocardial contractility during cardiogenic shock
Rapidly converting pulseless VT to a perfusing rhythm
Relaxing bronchial smooth muscle during acute wheezing

items.sourceUse: Selected rate/BP control and reduction of myocardial workload.
items.stem: Which treatment goal best matches prescribed metoprolol when blood pressure and conduction are suitable?
items.correct: Reducing tachycardia-related myocardial workload
alternatives: Raising systemic vascular resistance in vasodilatory shock
Rapidly reversing high-grade AV block with symptomatic bradycardia
Producing direct coronary vasodilation during acute nitrate rescue

items.sourceUse: Selected cardiovascular indications such as rate control, angina or BP treatment.
items.stem: Which patient problem most closely fits an appropriately selected propranolol prescription?
items.correct: Controlling symptomatic tachycardia without active bronchospasm
alternatives: Treating acute wheeze in a patient with uncontrolled asthma
Increasing cardiac output during profound low-output shock
Terminating ventricular fibrillation in cardiac arrest

items.sourceUse: Chronic BP control and antianginal therapy.
items.stem: Which clinical purpose best matches a daily oral amlodipine prescription?
items.correct: Long-term hypertension or angina control
alternatives: Immediate stabilization of a hypertensive emergency with organ injury
Direct reversal of an acute pulmonary embolism
Acute conversion of unstable ventricular tachycardia

items.sourceUse: Selected supraventricular arrhythmias/rate control and antianginal therapy.
items.stem: Which cardiovascular problem can fit an authorized verapamil regimen after rhythm and contraindication review?
items.correct: Selected supraventricular rate control with preserved perfusion
alternatives: Unstable wide-complex tachycardia needing immediate electrical therapy
Atrial fibrillation with known accessory-pathway pre-excitation
Symptomatic high-grade AV block with a slow escape rhythm

items.sourceUse: Chronic cardiovascular therapy for selected hypertension and heart-failure patients.
items.stem: Which ongoing treatment goal best matches oral enalapril after patient-specific BP, renal and potassium review?
items.correct: Long-term management of hypertension or selected heart failure
alternatives: Immediate pressor support during severe hypotensive shock
Rapid rhythm conversion during an unstable tachyarrhythmia
Acute removal of pulmonary fluid through loop diuresis

items.sourceUse: Secondary cardiovascular prevention, including after ACS.
items.stem: A patient has recovered from an acute coronary syndrome. Which goal best matches continued atorvastatin treatment?
items.correct: Lowering LDL and reducing future atherosclerotic events
alternatives: Immediately relieving an episode of ischemic chest pain
Preventing an imminent clot by direct platelet P2Y12 blockade
Rapidly dissolving a coronary thrombus during an acute MI

items.sourceUse: Chronic therapy for diabetes, heart failure and kidney disease depending on the patient.
items.stem: Which treatment goal fits continued dapagliflozin therapy in an appropriately selected stable patient?
items.correct: Reducing heart-failure or CKD risk even without a glucose-only indication
alternatives: Treating diabetic ketoacidosis as an emergency insulin substitute
Correcting severe hypoglycemia by rapid oral glucose delivery
Providing immediate diuretic rescue for flash pulmonary edema

items.sourceUse: Correction of hyperglycemia according to the current order/protocol.
items.stem: Which treatment goal describes a prescribed correction-insulin dose in a hospitalized patient?
items.correct: Addressing measured hyperglycemia according to an active dosing protocol
alternatives: Replacing all scheduled basal insulin in a patient who requires it
Treating suspected hypoglycemia before checking bedside glucose
Correcting ketoacidosis without an ordered insulin-fluid protocol

items.sourceUse: Selected hemodynamic support and some bradycardia pathways depending on protocol.
items.stem: Which emergency treatment goal can match prescribed dopamine infusion in an adult resuscitation setting?
items.correct: Support of selected symptomatic bradycardia when protocol alternatives are needed
alternatives: Conversion of ventricular fibrillation without defibrillation
Rate control of atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response
Routine kidney protection at low doses during sepsis

items.sourceUse: Acid suppression, stress-ulcer prophylaxis or GI-bleeding therapy when ordered.
items.stem: Which indication best matches prescribed pantoprazole in a hospitalized cardiac patient?
items.correct: Acid suppression for an indicated ulcer or GI-risk plan
alternatives: Increasing intestinal motility in gastroparesis
Treating immediate postoperative nausea via a dopamine receptor
Neutralizing an active anticoagulant after gastrointestinal bleeding

items.sourceUse: Acid suppression and GI protection according to the indication.
items.stem: Which clinical condition is most directly addressed by an appropriate omeprazole prescription?
items.correct: Gastric-acid suppression for a selected ulcer or reflux indication
alternatives: Acute vomiting caused by impaired gastric emptying
Severe upper GI bleeding requiring immediate clotting-factor replacement
Acute medication-induced constipation needing osmotic laxation

items.sourceUse: Anaerobic and selected protozoal infections according to the diagnosis.
items.stem: Which infection best matches a common metronidazole treatment role when prescribed and susceptibility supports it?
items.correct: A suspected intra-abdominal infection with anaerobic organisms
alternatives: A confirmed MRSA bloodstream infection requiring targeted monotherapy
A confirmed Pseudomonas pneumonia needing antipseudomonal therapy
A Candida bloodstream infection requiring systemic antifungal therapy

items.sourceUse: Mainly serious resistant Gram-positive infections including MRSA/VRE when prescribed.
items.stem: Which microbiological problem best supports selecting prescribed linezolid when an appropriate regimen is needed?
items.correct: A serious susceptible VRE or MRSA infection
alternatives: A pure infection due to susceptible Pseudomonas aeruginosa
A confirmed Candida bloodstream infection
A confirmed anaerobic gram-negative Bacteroides infection alone

items.sourceUse: Relief of bronchospasm/wheeze in the appropriate respiratory patient.
items.stem: Which respiratory presentation most directly supports a prescribed inhaled salbutamol dose?
items.correct: Acute wheeze with reversible bronchospasm
alternatives: New crackles due only to cardiogenic pulmonary edema without bronchospasm
Hypoxemia due only to a pulmonary embolism without airflow obstruction
Stridor from an upper-airway foreign body obstruction

items.sourceUse: Commonly used for oral candidiasis.
items.stem: Which presentation most closely matches the role of an oral nystatin preparation?
items.correct: Superficial oral candidiasis involving the mucosa
alternatives: Candida bloodstream infection requiring systemic treatment
Confirmed fungal meningitis requiring CNS-active treatment
Esophageal candidiasis requiring systemic antifungal therapy

items.sourceUse: Symptomatic treatment of vertigo/dizziness rather than a primary cardiac emergency drug.
items.stem: Which patient complaint most closely matches the symptomatic role of prescribed betahistine?
items.correct: Recurrent vestibular vertigo after an appropriate diagnosis
alternatives: Sudden vertigo with new unilateral weakness suggesting acute stroke
Syncope from a documented slow heart rhythm
Dizziness caused by measured severe hypoglycemia

policy: One revised form, reused unchanged for comprehensive/7-day/21-day
Do not regrade historical exam answers or claim full drug coverage
Source-derived roles, any external guideline variations require product/local protocol review
